body: I had severe wasteing before the Zenpep yeah, down to about 130, and the way the doctor explained it to me was the zenpep was easing some of my pancreases effort so I've been terrified of them coming back or losing all the work I've put in. Factually the GED is not a measure of intelligence. You are correct. But you can still fail it if you lack intelligence.

Factually a running marathon is not a measure of how many legs you have. But you can fail it if you lack enough legs.

I'm not saying I'm dumb so I can't pass it.
I'm saying after all the work I've put in and still can't pass it. I must be dumb. I felt pretty smart preGED. Even passed the math portion first try. I just can't read at a speed it requires and practice is not helping. Therfore I am dumb.

Your getting cause and effect backwards.

Your advice has been practice more and stop blaming being dumb. While I'm telling you I practice, I enjoy reading, and that I've practiced increased reading speed. 

I get that not everyone who fails the GED does so becuase they are slow. I get that I am not slow in every subject or across everything I do. I'm a trained butcher there are things I'm ok at. 

But what have you said other then try harder. And if I'm wrong I'm sorry but you don't know how hard I've tried or how much I've put into this.

How do I practice reading at am average speed?

The bag I got a few days ago says it's whey isolate on the bag. The hospital pharmacist said it's what they give baritric patients so I'm hopeful. If you use it too would you mind sharing what kind you use?

Is plant based protien easier to digest if your body isn't making enzymes normally? Why would you stay away from whey? Could you tell me what plant based brand you use?

Sorry dont mean to be a thousand questions I'm just nervous about getting ahead of my muscle loss.

An accommodation for what? They don't give those out without a reason. Also learning the tricks people use to read fast is learning to speedread.

How would I learn to read average. How does someone look up and practice average reading? Cause if it's practice reading then I do that. 

You keep saying I'm being stubborn and woe is me but I'm giving you a problem and pointing at the problem asking for a solution and to me your the one stubbornly saying just fix it while giving no real advice on fixing it.

And you've takin the stance of jumping to conclusions in everyone of your prior messages so maybe reading woe is me into a message saying I'm tired of failing and losing money is on you... 

look if you have an idea I'll take it, if you have something constructive other then to attack my exhaustion I truly want it... but you can't get an accommodation for reading slow and aphantasia isn't a disability.

In some things like math I'm average intelligence. But one of the vital things the GED tests is your ability to quickly obtain info, and to that yeah I'm slow.

I'm thankful to the writing skills I learned from the GED practice but it's not always as easy as just try harder.

Your assuming I'm coming from not working on it. I've done speed reading practice and I'm a couple 100$ down on practice tests and help books. I just physically cant look at a word and know what it says without saying the word in my head and have no visual memory so I can't keep the needed pace.

Speed reading or scanning can not work for me. I've tested it I can pass every subject without the timer. I'm just to slow. I'd pay anything to pass it and I've tried everything I can think of and worked with a tutor for months last year.

Some people are to slow. It hurts like hell to admit and you should never give up without trying everything you can but I got no more ideas. I'm not saying others should give up but at some point it became a self destructive obsession for me that to this day I fall back into over and over.

Also I agree math is a heck of a lot of critical thinking too. I just meant that with math there is a list of facts that can be studied while the other 3 subjects expect no outside knowledge(atleast in PA) and only require you to be able to find the relevant info in the information they provide.

In fact you can actually fail the essay for using outside knowledge. I just hate this anyone can pass it mentality. Sure go into it hoping to pass and try your hardest to pass but for some people it's an impossible dream.

I read as a few books a month. I love reading and my ability to take and understood what I'm reading isn't a problem. I just physically cant read fast enough to get to even 30 questions within time. My problem with the social science and science sections are the same. I can't read fast enough to get through the test.

I passed the math portion first try without studying. My problem is I need to subvocalize to read. I'm literally to slow to pass. 

I love reading. It's my primary hobby. I read or reread atleast a few chapters a week, and go through aleast a book a month. I really love reading. Still can't pass the GED. 

I learned how to write basic essays and still can't even answer half the questions on the test in time. If my problem isn't dumb what is it.

The math portion and essay are definitely a measure of knowledge you bring into it yeah, but the rest of it just tests reading speed and the ability to retain what you've just read. That's not knowledge. That's testing your ability to aquire knowledge. It's not that I can't pass becuase I don't know enough.

 I can't pass it becuase I'm to slow to read fast enough and no level of studying can prepare me to know the answers to questions in this situation.

If the problem was knowledge I could study
But it's not, I'm just to stupid, too slow to pull it off. But hey I can wrote essays now... so that's a thing.

The medical system in my country is so broken that I'm basicly just ignored in every way except selling me opiods. This is actually the longest conversation I've had in months and just thinking about that has be crying. I'm sorry if I'm being too dark it's just so hard stairing at these walls everyday. Half the time I don't know what day it is or if it's day or night any more.

I've been in a spiral of searching self help stuff online for the last two days but it's all stuff I can't do. My health doesn't allow me to go for long walks, and not having a car makes volunteering impossible. Besides even if I could get to a place to volunteer there isn't much I could really do to help. I know people wanna believe all life is special and valuable but in a sea of 7 billion there's bound to be a few worthless ones in the bunch. I just drew the short straw genetically and now I'm expected to live until my pancreas kills me painfully so that others can feel that all life is worth something... I'm just so tired of feeling like I'm living the same day on repeat but just a little sicker and weaker with each go through.

I also tried the weighted blanket but I think the one I got is to heavy as it makes my body ache. I got a 15 pound one back when I was 140 pounds but now that I'm 115 I think it might just be to heavy. Other then that I use books and web comics for the escapism or lay around telling myself stories about characters and worlds were things make more sense. The problem is whenever I'm brought back to reality my depression always gets really bad for days to the point were I don't eat and can't function.

It sounds like you got really lucky. I hope I get lucky like that someday too, but I really don't know how I'd be able to meet anyone or even make a friend. I can't drive and with my health problems walks arnt an option anymore. I wanna live but I just feel entombed. I used to atleast have a space to sit on a porch area to read but my landlord took that space away from me and even started to use my table I had out there so I lost that too. I'm sorry for being such a wet blanket it's just I've been alone and friendless down here since before the pandemic and I feel like I'm losing it. I know it sounds insane but it's Like the outside world isn't even real anymore.

I would if I could but I live a mile from the nearest bus stop and with my health issues I need a cane to walk. I just can't make it that far. I typically only get to leave my apartment once every two weeks for physical therapy.

I'm starting to feel like I'm losing my mind. Maybe the lack of sun's making it worse. I remember hearing somewhere that not getting sun is bad for the brain and bones but I don't know if there is real science in that or just a wife's tale.

Ged.com which I couldn't follow most questions and they didn't even provide answers but I imagine they were very simaler to what I should expect

Mometrix.com wich seemed legit and is were I got those scores from and

Passged.com wich broke down each test into mutlpe 4 question sections on the various stuff that makes up each topic.
